notes: Symmetric `preference_game` and `asymmetric_preference_game`. Each (i, j) block is sampled with the per-pair Batagelj-Brandes geometric-skip routine over a `vids_by_type` indirection table. As k grows at fixed n, per-block size shrinks quadratically while pair count grows triangularly, so total work decreases — visible in the type_count sweep (k=2: 1.5 ms vs k=8: 0.37 ms). The `fixed_sizes` variant skips the categorical-draw loop and is ~14% faster than the stochastic-assignment path at n=1000, k=4. The asymmetric variant uses a (no_out × no_in) joint cumulative distribution per vertex and visits every (out, in) pair via SBM's `PairShape` helper; loops=true adds 20% overhead because the (out, in) pair `(t, t)` for shared types samples a self-loop column that has to be remapped for the no-loops case. RNG state is not portable across implementations, so conformance asserts structural invariants only (vcount, directed flag, ecount band, is_simple, per-vertex types within range, diagonal-only-pref edge containment). Numbers from cargo bench --bench bench_preference -- --quick on Darwin/M-series release build.
